sentences.text: OP(MV) 1227/2012 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Manjeri is the appellant herein.

(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal).
2.
The petitioner filed the above O.P. under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 25.05.2012.

According to the petitioner, on 25.05.2012 at about 8 a.m., while he was traveling in a bus bearing registration No. KL-10-U-1575 driven by the 2nd respondent in a rash and negligent manner, the bus overturned and as a result of which he sustained serious injuries.
3. The 1st respondent is the owner and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
According to the petitioner, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The quantum of compensation claimed in the O.P. is Rs.90,01,000/- (claim limited to Rs.25,00,000/-).
4. The insurance company filed a written statement, admitting the accident as well as policy, but disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
5. The evidence in the case consists of the oral testimony of the petitioner as PW1 and Exts. A1 to A12 and X1.
No evidence was adduced by the respondents.
6. After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal awarded a total compensation of Rs.19,34,240/- (rounded to Rs.19,34,500/-).
7. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the appellant/ 3rd respondent preferred this appeal.
8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following: Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable.

9. Heard Sri. VPK. Panicker, the learned Standing Counsel appearing for the appellant, and Sri. K.
A. Salil Narayan, the learned Standing Counsel for the respondent/claimant.
The Point: In the accident the petitioner sustained Jon's fracture left, Fracture base of 3rd metatarsal, Punctured wound lateral aspect of left foot, Abrasion 3 x 3 cm left foot lateral aspect.
Initially he was admitted the Medical College Hospital, Calicut on 22.05.2012 to 28.5.2012 and he was on plaster for about 8 months.
Since there was no recovery from the injury sustained, he was admitted in Vellur Christian Medical College from 16.11.2013 to 19.11.2013.
Thereafter he was admitted in MES Medical College Hospital, Perinthalmanna from 02.05.2015 to 07.05.2015, to remove the implant fixed in Vellore Chirtian Medical College.

sentences.text: As per Ext.X1 Disability Certificate, issued by the Medical Board, General Hospital, Manjeri, his permanent physical disability was assessed as 36%.
The petitioner was a Heavy Driving License Holder and he claimed a monthly income of Rs.12,000/-.

The tribunal found that the petitioner was a Heavy Driving License Holder and found that because the injury sustained in the accident and the percentage of disability suffered by him, he could not continue his job as a driver as was done before, and fixed his functional disability at 50%.

The learned counsel for the 3rd respondent would argue that the Tribunal was not justified in fixing the functional disability at 50% as the permanent physical disability assessed by the medical board is only 36%.
12. In Ext.X1, the Medical Board noticed that on examination, the total analysis of left ankle at Neutral position (loss of dorsiflexion, plantar flexion arc, eversion - inversion arc).
Squatting possible but with difficulty, climbing stairs with difficulty.

The Tribunal relied upon the observations made by the Medical Board that the petitioner could squat and climb stairs only with difficulty, to come to the conclusion that he could not do the profession of driver anymore and fixed his functional disability at 50%.
The Tribunal has given valid and cogent reasons for fixing the functional disability of the petitioner at 50% and hence, I do not find any grounds to interfere with the same.
13. The Tribunal has fixed the monthly income of the petitioner at Rs.9,900/-.

The notional income of a coolie during the year 2012, in the light of the decisions in the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance 2025:KER:10388 Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], will come to Rs.8,500/-.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance 2025:KER:10388 Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the above circumstances, the monthly income of the petitioner fixed by the Tribunal at Rs.9,900/- cannot be said to be on the higher side.
Therefore, the monthly income of the petitioner fixed by the Tribunal at Rs.9,900/- is liable to be accepted.

14. Since the petitioner was aged 22 on the date of accident, 40% of the income is liable to be added towards future prospects, in the light of the dictum laid down by the decisions by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Co.Ltd v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680] and the multiplier to be applied is 18, in the light of the dictum in Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation, (2009)
6 SCC 121.

However, the Tribunal has committed a mistake by assessing the loss of disability at Rs.10,69,200/-, without adding 40%
income towards future prospects.

Therefore the loss of disability will be refixed as Rs.14,96,880/-.
15.
The learned counsel for the 3rd respondent would argue that the Tribunal has awarded two years' income under the head 2025:KER:10388 loss of earning which according to him is on the higher side.
Further he would argue that towards pain and suffering, the Tribunal has awarded Rs.1,00,000/- another Rs.1,00,000/- was awarded on the head loss of amenities.

Rs.50,000/- was awarded on the head future treatment, another Rs.50,000/- for deformity disfigurement and another Rs.2,00,000/- on the head loss of marriage prospects which according to him are on the higher side.

sentences.text: In this case, though the accident was on 22.05.2012 and the petitioner was discharged from the hospital on 28.05.2012, for the first eight months he was on plaster.
After removing the plaster, he was to be admitted in Vellur Christian Medical College for expert management.
From there, iron rod was fixed at the place of fracture.

Thereafter, he was again admitted in MES Hospital,
Perinthalmanna from 02.05.2015 to 07.05.2015 for removal of the implant.

That means his treatment in the Hospital lasted for about two years and as such there is merits in the finding of the Tribunal that the petitioner could not do his job as driver for a period of two years.
Therefore, the Tribunal were 2025:KER:10388 justified in awarding the income for a period of two years, towards loss of earnings.

17. It is true that the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- on the head loss of marriage prospects, Rs.50,000/- on the head deformity and disfigurement, Rs.50,000/- towards future treatment and Rs.1,00,000/- each on the heads loss of amenities and pain and suffering.

Considering the gravity of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and the period during which he was treated as inpatient and the period during which he had to take rest for removing the implant and for the reason that now he could squat and climb stairs only with difficulty, the compensation awarded on the heads pain and suffering and amenities are on the lower side.
At the same time, the compensation awarded on the heads disfigurement and loss of marriage prospects are on the higher side.
The compensation on the head future treatment cannot be treated as on the higher side.
Since the compensation awarded on the heads pain and suffering and loss of amenities are on the lower side.
I am not interfering with the compensation awarded on the heads disfigurement and loss of marriage prospects.
No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.
It appears that the Tribunal has awarded interest at the rate of 9% per annum.
Considering the facts, I hold that interest at the rate of 8% will be a reasonable one.
Therefore, the interest for the entire compensation will be at the rate of 8%.

19. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.23,61,920/-, as modified and recalculated above and given in the table below, for easy reference:

In the result, this Appeal is disposed off, directing the 3rd Respondent to deposit a total sum of Rs.23,61,920/- (Rupees Twenty Three Lakh Sixty One Thousand Nine Hundred and Twenty Only), less the amount already deposited, if any, along with interest at the rate of 8% per annum, from the date of the petition till deposit, within a period of two months from today.
21. On depositing the aforesaid amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the entire amount to the petitioner, excluding court fee payable, if any, without delay, as per rules.
